newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls bomb blasts in Israel troubling.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls bomb blasts in Israel troubling.

text.p: The United States extended condolences to the victims of two bomb blasts in Tel Aviv on Thursday and said it was "very troubling" that such violence had returned to Israel.

"We are not in a position to ascertain who caused it, we are unaware that there's been any formal claim of responsibility but we'll certainly keep close track of this," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.
"It's obviously very troubling that bomb blasts should return to Israel," Burns told reporters.

The blasts wounded at least 13 people near Tel Aviv's central bus station, Israeli officials said. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the bombings bore the hallmark of Palestinian "terrorist" attacks and vowed to respond with "extreme severity."
"The United States offers its sympathy to the victims and to their families," Burns said.

Burns said news of the blasts had arrived as U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, trying to negotiate an Israeli-Palestinian agreement on the town of Hebron, was meeting Netanyahu in Jerusalem. Netanyahu had been forced to break off the meeting as a result, he said.
